subject: sr-business-studies
title: External Trade
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of external trade?
questions.answer: D

questions.q: A shipping company asks for proof of delivery authorisation. The document to be shown is the —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Entrepot trade refers to —
options: importing goods and then re-exporting them without using them
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting is called —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The officials appointed by the government in its embassy to represent the country's trade interests are called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: A document prepared by the exporter or forwarding agent, on the basis of which customs calculates the export duty, is the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is another name for external trade?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The IEC number is granted by —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The form filled by the importer at the time of receiving goods, on which customs duty is calculated, is the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Foreign exchange for imports is released by the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Visible trade refers to the trade in —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which agent clears goods from the port of destination on behalf of the importer?
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) An importer cannot import goods without a valid import licence. (b) The exporter pays the import duty.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – the importer (through the clearing agent) pays import duty.

questions.q: Name the document: (a) An agreement signed with the shipping company to put goods on the ship. (b) Issued by the captain of the ship after loading.
questions.answer: (a) Shipping order. (b) Mate's receipt.

questions.q: Name the document: (a) Obtained by the forwarding agent from the shipping company after the mate's receipt. (b) An order placed for import of goods.
questions.answer: (a) Bill of lading. (b) Indent.

questions.q: Identify the official: (a) Provides guidance to exporters abroad on behalf of the government. (b) A form filled by the importer at the time of receiving the goods.
questions.answer: (a) Trade representative. (b) Bill of entry.

questions.q: State whether it is export, import or entrepot trade for India: (a) India bought goods from Russia and sold to Sri Lanka. (b) UK bought jewellery from India.
questions.answer: (a) Entrepot trade. (b) Export trade.

questions.q: Match: (a) Export houses (b) Indent houses (c) Clearing agents (d) Shipping company with (i) carries goods for freight (ii) receive orders with instructions (iii) clear goods at destination (iv) export promotion.
Give two examples of invisible trade.
questions.answer: Shipping and insurance services (also tourism, technician services).

questions.q: Expand: (i) IEC (ii) RCMC (iii) ECGC.
questions.answer: (i) Import Export Code. (ii) Registration-cum-Membership Certificate. (iii) Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Mention any two reasons for entrepot trade.
questions.answer: Non-accessibility of trade routes and goods needing processing or finishing (also lack of trade agreement).

questions.q: How does external trade improve the standard of living of people?
questions.answer: People consume goods they do not produce, and exports earn foreign exchange, raising income and living standards.

questions.q: How can a clearing agent help the importer?
questions.answer: He completes the customs and dock formalities, pays duty and takes delivery of the goods from the port and sends them to the importer.

questions.q: Define 'Letter of Credit'.
questions.answer: A document issued by the importer's bank in favour of the exporter assuring payment of the exporter's bill up to the specified amount.

questions.q: Explain visible and invisible trade.
questions.answer: Visible trade is import and export of goods; invisible trade is exchange of services such as shipping, insurance and tourism.

questions.q: State any four difficulties faced in external trade.
questions.answer: Geographical distance, greater risk, legal and customs restrictions and exchange rate fluctuations.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the three types of external trade.
questions.answer: Import trade (buying goods from a foreign country), export trade (selling goods to a foreign country) and entrepot trade (importing goods and re-exporting them).

questions.q: Explain any three roles played by a clearing agent in external trade.
questions.answer: Gets the bill of lading endorsed, files the bill of entry and pays customs duty; pays dock charges and takes delivery; despatches goods to the importer and sends advice.

questions.q: Explain any three documents used in external trade.
questions.answer: Bill of lading (issued by the shipping company), shipping bill (used by customs to compute export duty) and bill of entry (filed by the importer or clearing agent).

questions.q: Explain any three importance of external trade.
questions.answer: It promotes specialisation, improves living standards and generates employment.

questions.q: Explain any three facilitators of external trade.
questions.answer: Indent houses, forwarding agents and insurance companies (also shipping company and trade commissioners).

questions.q: Explain the difference between a letter of credit and a letter of hypothecation.
questions.answer: A letter of credit is issued by the importer's bank guaranteeing payment; a letter of hypothecation is given by the exporter to his bank authorising it to sell the goods if the bill is dishonoured.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the procedure for export trade.
questions.answer: Enquiry and quotation, indent, credit enquiry, export licence, procurement, inspection, excise clearance, packing, forwarding agent and shipping formalities, invoice and securing payment.

questions.q: Explain the procedure for import trade.
questions.answer: Trade enquiry, import licence, foreign exchange, indent, letter of credit, shipping documents, clearing agent, bill of entry, dock charges, despatch and advice.

questions.q: Explain the formalities completed by a forwarding agent.
questions.answer: Customs permit, shipping order, shipping bill and export duty, dock dues, customs verification, mate's receipt, bill of lading, insurance and advice to the exporter.

questions.q: Explain the difficulties faced in external trade.
questions.answer: Distance, risk, transport problems, customs restrictions, market study, changing rules and exchange rate fluctuations.

questions.q: Explain the importance of external trade.
questions.answer: Specialisation, standard of living, competition, employment, price equalisation, international relations, economic growth and resource utilisation.
